channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI Influencers Are Trying to Shape Brazil’s Presidential Election
item.description: Synthetic creators can build communities around shared political views
item.dc:creator: Beatriz Reis

item.title: Hugging Face Unveils $400 Singing, Skating Duck-Like Robot
item.description: Artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face Inc. unveiled a singing $400 bipedal robot that can be taught tricks, the latest in the company’s ongoing effort to make AI and robotics more approachable to the general public.The cute robot — aptly named Microduck — takes clear inspiration from its namesake bird, except that it has only one eye. It will go on sale later this year, Hugging Face said Thursday, making it the second robot from the company.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Kelly and Natalie Lung

item.title: Meta’s Teen Safeguards on Facebook, Instagram Apply Only to US
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s changes to Instagram and Facebook, part of a series of landmark settlements to resolve claims that the social media networks are a safety risk to children, will apply only to US users for now.
item.dc:creator: Newley Purnell and Gian Volpicelli

item.title: Putin Moves to Escalate War in Ukraine, Nvidia Fuels Faith in AI Boom | Opening Trade 8/27/2026
item.description:
Russia is preparing to escalate attacks on Ukraine after concluding that negotiations for a peace deal have reached a dead end, according to three people close to the Kremlin. For now, Russia is weighing an intensification of powerful conventional ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv, including the center of the capital, and infrastructure targets in other Ukrainian cities, the people said, asking not to be identified because the matter is sensitive.
Nvidia, the chipmaker at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, gave a bullish sales outlook for fiscal 2028, easing concerns that AI spending is poised to lose momentum.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Germany Running Short of AI Compute Capacity, Minister Says
item.description: Germany’s top digital policy official said surging demand for artificial intelligence is putting a squeeze on data centers in Europe’s largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou and Anna Edwards

item.title: Stripe Says AI Helps Asian Firms Expand Globally at Record Pace
item.description: Artificial intelligence is enabling Asian businesses to expand globally at unprecedented speed, Sarita Singh, Stripe Inc.’s managing director for Southeast Asia, Greater China and South Korea, said in an interview on Bloomberg Television.
item.dc:creator: Haslinda Amin

item.title: China’s Spirit AI bets on smarter robot brains
item.description: Spirit AI CEO Han Fengtao says robots can already handle office tasks “unimaginable half a year ago,” from delivering paper to shredding documents. He told Bloomberg’s Minmin Low that “the evolution of the robot brain will get faster and faster,” predicting a “ChatGPT moment” within three years. With several hundred units deployed in China, Spirit AI is betting on smarter robot brains to drive large‑scale adoption across industries — and eventual global expansion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ebola Vaccine Race Expands as Congo Bundibugyo Outbreak Grows
item.description: Efforts to develop a vaccine against the strain of Ebola driving the deadly outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo are expanding, with an experimental shot developed by an Egypt-based pharmaceutical company set to advance toward human testing.
item.dc:creator: Jason Gale

item.title: Cheap Tokens, Costly Chips and a Missing AI Payoff
item.description: The price of AI is collapsing, while the cost of building it is not. Equity investors have spent the summer trying to work out who gets caught in between.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Patrick Barnert

item.title: ‘Locker King’ Billionaire Pushes Poland to Take Meta Fight to EU
item.description: Poland is pushing for a European Union probe into Meta Platforms Inc. following a years-long campaign by InPost SA billionaire Rafal Brzoska over fraudulent ads on its services.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski

item.title: Nvidia's Upbeat Sales Outlook Eases Concerns About AI Economy
item.description: Nvidia, the chipmaker at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, said it forecasts revenue growth of about 70% in fiscal 2028. Analysts had predicted 45%. The upbeat outlook offered relief to investors concerned about a bubble in the AI economy. Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Greatland Resources MD Shaun Day on Earnings
item.description: Shaun Day, Managing Director at Greatland Resources, discusses the gold and copper producer's full-year results, which saw its annual profit more than double. He also discusses its outlook for output in fiscal 2027. He speaks exclusively with Haidi Stroud-Watts on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lopez: AI Biggest Infrastructure Upgrade Since Internet
item.description: Nvidia, the chipmaker at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, gave a bullish sales outlook for fiscal 2028, easing concerns that AI spending is poised to lose momentum. Maribel Lopez, Founder & Enterprise AI Lead at Lopez Research, spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa on the rising tide of AI in tech. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Probes Singapore Firm Over Alleged Nvidia Chip Smuggling
item.description: The US government is investigating Singapore-based Apex Logistics for its suspected role in smuggling Nvidia Corp. AI chips to China, people familiar with the matter said, in what may result in the first action against a transportation company for allegedly participating in the illegal semiconductor trade.
item.dc:creator: Kari Lindberg and Mackenzie Hawkins

item.title: US Says China-Linked Hackers Targeted NASA, Fed and Senate
item.description: The US Justice Department said authorities disrupted online infrastructure allegedly used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers to target American government agencies and critical infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: India Says 288 Nationals Unreachable After Nepal Floods
item.description: India said as many as 288 of its nationals, including workers at a power project, remain unreachable after catastrophic flash floods swept through Nepal.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey and Akriti Sharma

item.title: Kioxia, Sandisk Plan $31 Billion Japan Memory Chip Expansion
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. and Sandisk Corp. plan to spend more than ¥5 trillion ($31.4 billion) to ratchet up production capacity in Japan, boosting output of a critical AI data center component that’s in short supply.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Mochizuki and Hideki Suzuki

item.title: UK Starts Selling Plug-In Solar at Argos to Lower Bills
item.description: The UK will become the latest European country to sell plug-in solar panels, with Argos Ltd. and UKSOL Ltd. offering them as early as Thursday and other shops following in the coming weeks.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Shankleman and Petra Sorge

item.title: Nvidia Sees AI-Fueled Demand Boosting Sales 70% Next Year
item.description: Nvidia Corp., the chipmaker at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, said revenue will grow about 70% next fiscal year, easing concerns that AI spending is poised to lose momentum.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Z.ai’s Shares Soar After Claiming Surprise AI Hit Ox Alpha
item.description: China’s Z.AI Co. confirmed it’s responsible for the Ox Alpha AI model that swept to the top of online usage charts this weekend, pushing its shares up as much as 12% on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
